title: The Even Share
logline: At dawn, a beach-seine crew hauls in the night's catch and divides it by a traditional share system that everyone on the beach knows by heart. Every division is a small, quick test of what the crew will and won't hold back.

object.note: Object 3 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The night's watch ends at dawn; on a southern beach another dawn's work, a hauled net, is divided into shares, and each division is a quick test of what is held back.

thread_out.thread: What is held back moves from the catch to a skill: a family workshop that teaches an outsider, but not everything.

requirements: A beach-seine fishing community that still practises a traditional share system
A crew willing to be filmed through a full haul and division
Predawn or dawn access to the beach

lesson.in_simple_terms: Holding on to what is ours can feel less like enjoying it and more like a small sting when it has to be shared. The texts notice this and group that kind of holding back with anger, not with wanting.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අපේ දේ බෙදාගන්නට සිදුවන විට දැනෙන මසුරුකම ඇල්මෙන් හටගත්තත්, එය එළියට එන්නේ නොසතුටක් ලෙස නිසා ධර්මය එය තරහ පැත්තට ගණන් කරයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Stinginess (macchariya) is not bearing one's own things to pass to others, to benefit others, or to be matched by what others receive, and one of its five kinds concerns gain. Margaya explains a fine point: although it springs from attachment to one's own things, it shows itself as displeasure at their being shared, so it arises with aversion and never with greed. Pradeepika adds that envy (issā) looks at other people's good fortune, while stinginess looks at one's own.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The haul is shared work, bodies pulling in rhythm; then the catch is laid on the sand and divided, basket by basket, under a system everyone knows by heart. Each division is a small moment where ease, or a flicker of reluctance, can show in a face or a pause, and the film records whichever actually happens, including any share set aside for people beyond the crew.
lesson.caution: This does not mean the crew are stingy or that anyone's mind can be read from the outside; the teaching is about single moments of mind, and easy fairness is just as likely to be what the camera sees.
lesson.builds_on: After a night where aversion showed as fear of an outside threat, this film turns inward: the same displeasure can hide inside holding on to what is already ours.
